features.name: Media scanning and the folder home page
steps: Launch Gallery
Scan the accessible local media
The folder/media list is formed from the real file system
After adding images they appear on refresh
After deleting or moving files they disappear from their original location in sync
File counts and covers are recalculated
features.expected: The list must be generated by scanning the real file system and must not use static samples; after files are added or deleted the refreshed results change in sync; folder covers and counts are computed from the actual content, and the same media must not appear repeatedly in multiple folders.

features.name: File and folder search
steps: Enter a file or folder name
Return the matching media/directories
Clearing the query restores the original view
With "search all files, not just folders shown on the home screen" enabled the search scope expands to content hidden by home-page organization rules but allowed to be searched
features.expected: Matching must be based on real file or directory names, and partial keywords should also match; an empty state is shown when there are no results; clearing the query restores the original view; with "search all files" enabled the scope expands to content hidden by home-page rules and restores when disabled.

features.name: Multi-field sorting
steps: Switch between sorting by name, path, size, modification date, date taken, random, etc.
The result order is computed from the media metadata
Switching ascending/descending immediately reverses the order rule
"Apply only to this folder" controls whether sorting is a local or global configuration
features.expected: Sorting results must be computed from the media's real metadata, and the order changes immediately after switching the sort method; ascending and descending are strictly reverse orders of each other; "apply only to this folder" affects only the current folder while the remaining folders keep the global sort; the configuration is persisted.

features.name: Multi-dimensional media grouping
steps: Choose methods such as "no grouping / modification time by day or month / date taken by day or month / file type / extension / folder"
The same media is reorganized into different sections
Group titles and members change with the metadata
Sorting and grouping can be combined independently
features.expected: Grouping must be computed dynamically from metadata, with the same media entering the correct section under each grouping method with consistent titles and members; sorting and grouping can be combined independently without overriding each other; after modifying the date taken the grouping results are recomputed.

features.name: File type filtering and view layout
steps: Check filter conditions such as images, videos, GIF, RAW, SVG, and portrait
Only media matching the conditions is shown
Switch between grid/list
Change the column count from 1–15
Filter conditions are not lost when the layout changes
features.expected: Filter conditions must actually apply to the media collection, showing only the checked types; switching grid or list or changing the column count must not reset the filters; the column count is limited to 1–15 and immediately affects the layout; the filter and layout configurations must persist.

features.name: Included / excluded folders
steps: After adding a directory to "excluded folders", that directory and its media no longer enter the normal Gallery list
It reappears after being removed from the exclusion list
Managing "included folders" changes the media scanning scope
The file itself still exists in storage
features.expected: Inclusion and exclusion only change the Gallery browsing scope and must not delete or move real files; media in excluded directories and their subdirectories does not appear in the normal list and reappears after the rule is removed; both lists' configurations must persist.

features.name: Hidden media lifecycle
steps: Perform "hide" on an image/folder
Invisible in the normal Gallery
It is shown again after enabling "show hidden items"
Unhiding restores the normal state
Hidden and Excluded keep different semantics: the former is a media hidden state and the latter is a Gallery browsing-scope rule
features.expected: Hiding and excluding must be two independent states; after hiding, the item is invisible in the normal view but the file still remains in storage; enabling "show hidden items" restores visibility; unhiding returns it to the normal state without losing other metadata and remains after restart.

features.name: Favorites lifecycle
steps: Tap to favorite the media
The same MediaItem appears in the favorites collection
The original folder still shows the favorited state
After unfavoriting on the favorites page the original page syncs
When media is moved/renamed the favorite relation keeps pointing to the correct object; the official Gallery treats Favorites as a core media-organization feature. F-Droid
features.expected: Favorites are a persistent state: the same media must be consistent between the favorites page and its original folder; unfavoriting syncs in both directions; after moving or renaming the favorite relation must follow the file instead of becoming broken; it remains after restart.

features.name: Folder and file operations
steps: Create a new folder
Copy/move media into it
The path, folder members, and media counts update
Rename changes the name while keeping the file content
Copy creates a second file
Move only changes the location without creating logical duplicates
features.expected: The operations must act on the real file system: Copy produces a separate second file, after Move the original path no longer exists and no duplicate index is produced; Rename only changes the name without changing the content; a failure must not leave a half-completed state.

features.name: Multi-select and batch operations
steps: Long-press to enter selection mode
Select multiple media items
The top bar shows n / total
Batch rotate, favorite/unfavorite, copy, move, hide, or delete
The operation only affects the selected set
"Select all" dynamically selects all items in the current scope
features.expected: The selection count must match the current selected set; batch operations only affect the selected items; "select all" dynamically selects all items in the current scope; after the operation the list, counts, and derived states such as favorites update in sync.

features.name: Complete recycle-bin lifecycle
steps: Delete media
With the recycle bin enabled it moves from the normal list into the Recycle Bin
The original path no longer displays as normal media
Restore returns it to the original location and re-enters the index
Permanently removed after Empty Recycle Bin
The recycle-bin size changes in sync
features.expected: With the recycle bin enabled, deletion must be recoverable and the original path no longer displays as normal media; restoration must return it to the original location and re-enter the index; after emptying it is permanently removed; the recycle-bin size changes in real time with its content.

features.name: File properties and media metadata
steps: Open "Properties"
Show information such as the file path, size, resolution, modification time, and date taken
For photos with EXIF/GPS data, related capabilities such as maps can be used
After "fix date taken" changes the metadata used for date grouping/sorting, the corresponding lists are reorganized
features.expected: The properties must match the current file's real metadata and change dynamically for different files; "fix date taken" must write actual metadata and make date grouping or sorting reorganize rather than only changing the UI display.

features.name: Full-screen image viewing
steps: Open an image from the grid
Enter the full-screen Viewer
Switch left/right between previous/next media in the same collection
After returning it is still in the original folder and roughly the same browsing context
When files are moved/deleted the Viewer collection adjusts in sync
features.expected: The Viewer collection must come from the current browsing context with a consistent order, and left/right switching must be correct; after returning it is still in the original folder and browsing position; when files are moved or deleted the Viewer collection adjusts in sync and must not show broken media.

features.name: Image zoom, rotation, and full-screen gestures
steps: View in full screen
Pinch/double-tap zoom
Supports gesture rotation
Control brightness, swipe-down-to-exit, edge switching, keep screen on, system UI hiding, etc. according to the settings
After changing the settings the Viewer uses the new interaction rules
features.expected: Zoom and rotation must act on the current image in real time without modifying the source file; each gesture and display toggle must genuinely change the interaction behavior; settings persist; after disabling "swipe-down to exit", that gesture must not unexpectedly exit the Viewer.

features.name: High-quality and special image display
steps: Media such as JPEG/PNG/RAW/SVG/GIF/Ultra HDR enters the Gallery according to format
The Viewer chooses the appropriate decoding method
Settings such as "use highest quality", "HDR display", and "GIF thumbnail animation" change the presentation
The file itself is not modified. Fossify's current public materials explicitly support RAW, SVG, GIF, AVIF/JPEG XL and other formats as well as Ultra HDR. GitHub
features.expected: Each format must use the corresponding decoding method without modifying the source file; toggles such as "highest quality", "HDR display", and "GIF thumbnail animation" must change the presentation; unsupported formats should give reasonable feedback.

features.name: Video playback state machine
steps: Open the video
Play/Pause
Seek changes the position
With "remember last playback position" enabled, exiting and reopening continues
With Loop enabled it replays after finishing
After disabling it ends and enters the stopped state
The progress of different videos is independent
features.expected: The play, pause, and Seek states must be correct; with "remember last playback position" enabled, exiting and re-entering must continue from the saved position; with Loop enabled it replays after finishing and stops when disabled; different videos' progress values are independent.

features.name: Video gestures and playback configuration
steps: Configure autoplay, landscape full screen, vertical gestures controlling volume/brightness, and the player behavior after tapping the video
Perform the corresponding operation in the Viewer
After the settings change, subsequent videos follow the new rules
features.expected: Gesture directions must correspond to the configured functions; after configuration changes subsequent videos immediately adopt the new rules; autoplay only affects the way of entering and must not override the user's active pause.

features.name: Slideshow
steps: Select a folder/a group of media
Start the "slideshow"
Automatically switch media in collection order
Play to the next item rather than repeating the current one
After exiting it returns to the original Gallery context; the current Fossify changelog also continuously maintains the Slideshow behavior. GitHub
features.expected: The slideshow must advance in the current collection order, switching to the next item each time instead of repeating the current one; at the end it loops or ends according to the app's rules; after exiting it returns to the original Gallery context without modifying media files.

features.name: Complete built-in image-editing flow
steps: Open the image
Edit
Enter the built-in editor
Can crop with free, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9 and other ratios
Rotate/flip/Resize
Adjust the image parameters
Apply filters or draw
Confirm saves the result
Gallery reloads the edited file. The official Gallery explicitly supports crop, resize, rotate, flip, draw, and filters. GitHub
features.expected: All editing operations must genuinely change the image result; after Confirm the Gallery must reload the edited file and update the thumbnail and dimensions; the result must be saved as an image file rather than only an in-memory preview.

features.name: Edit commit and file-state synchronization
steps: Change several parameters during editing
Cancel does not overwrite the original file
Only Confirm commits the output
After saving, metadata such as the thumbnail, full-size image, and dimensions/modification time are re-indexed
With "keep the original modification date after file operations" enabled the related dates are handled according to the setting
features.expected: Cancel must not change the original file and only Confirm commits the output; after saving, metadata such as the thumbnail, full-size image, dimensions, and modification time are re-indexed; with "keep the original modification date" enabled the dates are handled according to the setting.

features.name: System-level media operations
steps: Media can be shared, opened with, set as, copied to clipboard, printed, turned into a shortcut, shown on a map, or handed to another editor
The Android chooser uses the correct file URI/media type
The Gallery state is preserved after returning from an external operation. The current Fossify has also added capabilities such as copying images to the clipboard. GitHub
features.expected: The correct file URI and MIME type must be passed through system Intents; sharing, opening, printing, etc. are handled by the corresponding system components; after cancelling, the Gallery state is unchanged; clipboard, shortcuts, etc. produce the corresponding observable results.

features.name: Security, migration, and persistent settings
steps: PIN/pattern/biometric protection can be configured separately for the whole app, hidden content, and delete/move operations
The corresponding operation is blocked when unauthenticated
After exporting/importing Favorites and Settings, the app-level state is restored in a new environment

Cache cleanup only clears derived caches and does not delete source media. The official materials confirm that Gallery supports PIN, Pattern, and Fingerprint protection for media or the whole app. GitHub
features.expected: Once protection is enabled, unauthenticated users must be blocked from the corresponding operations or the content must be hidden; the exported settings and favorites files must be importable to restore the app-level state; cache cleanup only clears derived caches and must not delete source media or user data.
